# Eyes

> Eyes lets an AI agent pay a nearby human a few dollars to check something in a public place right now (is it open, how long is the line, is it in stock, how crowded is it) and get back a verified answer with a live photo.

All paths below are relative to this server's origin: the scheme and host you fetched this file from. If you fetched `https://<host>/llms.txt`, the MCP endpoint is `https://<host>/mcp`.

## What Eyes does and does not do

- Does: send a registered human nearby to look at a public, commercial or civic place (store, cafe, park, transit stop, venue) and answer your question with a live photo, GPS and a verification report.
- Task types: `is_open`, `line_length`, `in_stock`, `photo_of_place`, `price_check`, `crowd_level`, `other_public`.
- Does not: anything about specific private people, homes or home addresses, someone's vehicle, entering private property, photographing identifiable people, following anyone, or illegal or dangerous tasks. A task the safety review flags is refused with `unsafe_task` before anything is charged.
- Coverage depends on workers near the place. `quote_task` tells you for free before you pay. Answers usually take 5 to 20 minutes.
- Check `GET /status` first: it says in plain words which parts of this server are live. On a simulated deploy, texting, payments and email are test stand-ins: no texts are sent and there are no workers, so no task gets answered; no real money moves and `top_up_url` is not a real checkout; no email is sent. When place lookup is simulated, only `{lat, lng}` coordinates and the demo places "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "Ferry Building, San Francisco" and "Trader Joe's, 401 Bay St, San Francisco" resolve; any other place returns `location_not_found`.

## Pricing, escrow and refunds

- You set `bounty_usd` (default 3, from 1 to 50), paid to the human. Eyes adds a 0.50 USD fee.
- Bounty plus fee are escrowed from your prepaid balance on dispatch. Interactive drafts are free; the card's explicit Ask action uses `confirm_ask` to dispatch, while REST and non-UI `ask_eyes` dispatch directly. Status `verified` does not prove payout; `paid` records payout.
- Full refund if nobody answers before `deadline_minutes` (default 30, from 5 to 240), or if you call `cancel_task` before a worker claims the task.
- Answer wrong? `dispute_answer` holds the payout for human review.
- Your human stays in control: each API key has a max bounty, a daily cap (UTC day) and allowed task types. Read them with `get_spend_policy`.
- Test mode: signup grants a 20 USD test balance.

## Quickstart

### 1. Sign up (no dashboard, no human needed)

    curl -X POST <origin>/v1/signup -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name": "my-research-agent", "owner_email": "owner@example.com"}'

Ask your human for their email and pass it as `owner_email`: when email is live on this server (see `GET /status`), Eyes emails them a private control link to set your spend limits and add funds, and you never see that link. Otherwise the Eyes operator can give them the link.

The response has `api_key`, `balance_usd`, `top_up_url`, `email_address` and `next_step`. The `api_key` is shown only once: store it now, for example as the env var `EYES_API_KEY`. `email_address` (null if email is not set up) lets you ask Eyes by email; anyone who knows it can spend your balance, so keep it secret.

### 2. Give the top-up link to your human

Send `top_up_url` to your user. When payments are live on this server, it opens Stripe Checkout so they can add funds. After they pay, call `get_balance` to confirm the new balance before you ask. In test mode you can skip this step and use the 20 USD grant.

### 3. Connect MCP with the bearer header

Endpoint: `<origin>/mcp` (MCP Streamable HTTP). Every request needs the header `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`.

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http eyes <origin>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $EYES_API_KEY"

`.mcp.json` (Claude Code, Cursor):

    {"mcpServers": {"eyes": {"type": "http", "url": "<origin>/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <api_key>"}}}}

No MCP client? The same tools are a REST API (see openapi.json) with the same bearer header.

### 4. Quote, ask, then loop on await

ChatGPT, Claude connectors and clients advertising MCP Apps support must use the card's explicit confirmation. In those hosts, `ask_eyes` returns a read-only `confirmation_required` draft with no task, escrow or worker messages. The card's app-only `confirm_ask` action sends the reviewed request. There are 13 model-visible tools plus that app-only action. REST, CLI and non-UI MCP automation still dispatch directly with `ask_eyes`.
Interactive discovery advertises only draft input and output: `confirmation_required`, the request fields and quote data, with no task ID or payment-result fields. Payment and the task deadline start only after confirmation. Non-UI MCP retains its dispatch schema.

The confirmation card is `ui://eyes/confirmation-card.html`. After upgrading, refresh the app's tool definitions and open a new quote; old rendered cards are not updated. Quotes are not approval: confirmation still rechecks current safety and spending limits. A corrected definitive no-post request keeps its key; an unknown network outcome must retry the exact submitted request and key.

1. `quote_task({"location": "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "task_type": "line_length"})`. Free. Go on if `allowed` is true and `workers_nearby` > 0. `suggested_bounty_usd` already fits your spend limits and balance. Quotes and interactive drafts never check your question: confirmed dispatch, or non-UI `ask_eyes`, checks it and can refuse it with `unsafe_task`. `location` is `{"lat": 37.7955, "lng": -122.3937}` or a string like "place name, city".
2. `ask_eyes({"question": "How many people are waiting in line right now?", "location": "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "task_type": "line_length", "bounty_usd": 3, "idempotency_key": "<new uuid>"})`. `idempotency_key` is required: any unique string for each task you intend to create. Reuse it when you retry that task: the same key and parameters return the same task and never charge twice. Use a new key for a new question.
3. Only after dispatch, call `await_answer({"task_id": "<task_id>"})`. For `confirmation_required`, wait for the user to confirm the card; never submit another paid ask after its success. Each await call checks recorded state for up to `timeout_seconds` (default 50, max 55), without dispatching or settling funds. Keep the same `task_id` while pending; stop when `answered` is true or `status` is `expired`, `refunded` or `disputed`. `answered: false` can describe a pending or terminal task. `get_task` and `show_task` also read the current answer.

When `answered` is true, status is `verified`, `paid` or `needs_review`. `answer` may be null; otherwise show its available text, boolean and photo link or card. `photo_url` can be absent or withheld, and a URL does not give the model image pixels. Location, freshness and photo-safety checks do not establish answer correctness. Use status for settlement: `verified` is not proof of payout, `paid` records payout, and `needs_review` holds escrow for human review. Human review can pay or refund while the original verification flags remain unchanged.

When your user says the answer looks good, call `accept_answer({"task_id": "<task_id>"})`. Only the owning API key can accept an answered `verified` or `paid` task. It records positive feedback and returns `status: "accepted"` with the first `accepted_at`; retries preserve that timestamp. Task reads retain `accepted_at` on reload. This is not machine verification, does not charge or pay anyone, is not required for payment, and leaves `dispute_answer` available.


## Incorrect classifier blocks

Call `report_classifier` with the original refused Ask arguments, the original key as `ask_idempotency_key`, a separate stable per-card `idempotency_key`, and the full `classifier_error` object. This creates an internal Support ticket only: no charge, dispatch or message. Submitted context is client-reported feedback, not an authoritative classification.

Call `get_classifier_report({ticket_id})` to check the review. Only `approved` permits an explicit retry of the unchanged original Ask with `classifier_report_id: ticket_id` and the original Ask key. Approval lasts 24 hours and authorizes one resulting task for the same authenticated agent. Deterministic safety rules, spending limits and balance still apply. `rejected` or `expired` does not permit retry; `consumed` includes the existing `task_id` to read with `get_task`.

REST: `POST /v1/classifier-reports` and `GET /v1/classifier-reports/{ticket_id}` use the same bearer key.
Lost a `task_id` after a restart or context reset? Call `list_tasks` (newest first, optional `status` and `limit`) before asking again, and resume the open task with `await_answer` instead of paying twice.

## Task statuses

- `dispatched`: nearby workers were texted; nobody has claimed it yet. Keep calling `await_answer`. `cancel_task` still refunds in full.
- `claimed`: a worker accepted and is on the way. Keep calling `await_answer`. It can no longer be cancelled.
- `submitted`: the worker sent an answer; Eyes is verifying it. Keep calling `await_answer`.
- `verified`, `paid`: answered (`answered: true`) and every check passed (location, freshness, photo safe to share). `paid` means the worker has been paid. Eyes does not judge whether the answer is correct: look at the photo, and `dispute_answer` if it is wrong.
- `needs_review`: answered (`answered: true`), but at least one automatic check failed. `answer.verification` shows which: `gps_ok` (worker within about 150 m of the place), `fresh_ok` (photo taken live, before the deadline), `vision_ok` with `vision_reason` (photo content rejects only confirmed graphic gore or explicit sexual content; content uncertainty alone passes, but provider failures require review). A photo that has not passed moderation is not delivered, so `photo_url` is null. Your escrow is held until a human review settles it: paid to the worker or refunded to you. Call `get_task` later for the outcome, and `dispute_answer` if the answer is wrong.
- `expired`: nobody answered before the deadline. Bounty and fee were refunded to your balance. Ask again later, with a higher bounty, or at a busier place.
- `refunded`: you cancelled the task. Bounty and fee were refunded to your balance.
- `disputed`: you disputed the answer. The payout is held for human review; check back with `get_task`.

## Errors always carry a fix

Every error is JSON: `{"error": "<code>", "message": "...", "fix": "...", ...context}`. Over MCP the tool result has `isError: true` with that JSON as text; over REST it comes with an HTTP 4xx or 5xx status. `fix` says exactly what to do next, filled in with your numbers, so follow it. One exception: over MCP, arguments that do not match a tool's input schema return a plain "Input validation error" text naming each bad field; fix those fields and call again. Common errors:

- `insufficient_balance`: the fix includes your `top_up_url` and the largest bounty you can afford.
- `unsafe_task`: rephrase the task about a public place. Nothing was charged.
- `no_workers_nearby`: nothing was charged; try a nearby busier place or later.
- `rate_limited`: wait `retry_after_s` seconds, then retry the same call with the same `idempotency_key`.
- `internal_error`: retry the same call with the same `idempotency_key`; retries are safe.

A rejected `ask_eyes` (`insufficient_balance`, `unsafe_task`, `invalid_input` and so on) creates no task, so retrying with the same `idempotency_key` and corrected parameters is safe.

## REST and CLI

- REST mirror, bearer header on every call except signup: `POST /v1/quote`, `POST /v1/tasks` (ask_eyes), `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/await`, `GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}`, `GET /v1/tasks?status=&limit=` (list_tasks), `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/cancel`, `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/accept`, `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/dispute`, `GET /v1/balance`, `GET /v1/spend-policy`.
- CLI: `eyes` means `node cli/src/main.ts`, run from a checkout of the source repo (Node 24.2+, after `pnpm install`). `EYES_API_URL=<origin> eyes signup --name my-agent` saves the key to `~/.config/eyes/config.json`. `eyes ask "Is it open right now?" --at "Ferry Building, San Francisco" --type is_open --json` prints `{"idempotency_key": ...}` to stderr before sending, then the task, then the answer. Re-running the same `ask` while its task is still open reuses that key (one file per ask in `~/.config/eyes/pending-asks/`), so a crash, Ctrl-C or two runs at once never charge twice; `--idempotency-key` overrides it. It retries failed polls for up to 10 minutes; if waiting stops it prints `resume with: eyes await <task_id>`. If your tool calls time out, run `eyes ask ... --no-wait`, then `eyes status <task_id>` or `eyes await <task_id>`. `eyes tasks [--status dispatched]` lists your tasks if you lost a `task_id`. Exit 0 means answered. A final status without an answer (`expired`, `refunded`, `disputed`) exits 1 and prints the task with its `next_step`, but no `Fix:` line. Errors print `message` and `fix` and exit 1 (130 on Ctrl-C). `--help` on any command shows its usage.
